entities.summary:
Lucius Valerius Catullus Messalinus was a Roman senator during the Flavian dynasty, and is best known as the most hated and ruthless delator or informer of his age. He was feared all the more due to his blindness.

Born into a prominent family, Messalinus rose to prominence through his connections to the Roman elite, including the emperor Domitian. His rise to power was marked by a series of strategic alliances and calculated risks, which ultimately earned him the nickname 'Delator' among his contemporaries.

Messalinus's most infamous achievement was his role in the persecution of Christians, which led to the deaths of thousands of innocent people. His actions were motivated by a desire for power and influence, as well as a twisted sense of morality.

Despite his notorious reputation, Messalinus's legacy is complex and multifaceted. His actions had a profound impact on the development of Christianity, and his influence can still be felt in modern politics and society.

The annals of history are filled with examples of individuals who have left their mark on the world. But few have been as thoroughly reviled as Lucius Valerius Catullus Messalinus, a name that evokes fear, hatred, and disgust in equal measure.
